# From CTR to satisfaction and uplift: define the supervision before sharing parameters

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-29 · 36 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

ESMM constrains click-to-conversion funnel probabilities. MMoE and PLE decide how tasks share experts. FLVM distinguishes consumption, active engagement, and positive versus negative direction. Incrementality compares potential outcomes with and without an action. More prediction heads, more shared parameters, or extra latent factors do not establish causal identification.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Sharing does not replace label semantics

ESMM defines CTR, conditional CVR, and joint CTCVR. MMoE and PLE determine how those or other tasks share parameters. Labeling every non-click a conditional CVR negative is wrong even with PLE, and a correct probability chain does not remove gradient conflicts. Audit label definitions, observability, and sharing separately.

Sources: [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md) · [Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts](../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en.md) · [Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en.md)

### Separating measurement factors does not prove uplift

FLVM separates watching, active engagement, and positive/negative direction using a constrained baseline and three-factor routing, avoiding the assumption that watching a long video means liking it. Incrementality compares potential outcomes with and without action. Better observational proxies for satisfaction cannot replace a credible control for counterfactual decisions.

Sources: [Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en.md) · [From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en.md) · [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

KL-MOPD locates competition between clicks and value at SID positions rather than combining only item-level scores. Initial-student KL discrepancies to both teachers are calibrated once and frozen; the current student computes weighted reverse KL on its own prefixes. This is not adaptive reweighting by current KL or averaging teacher probabilities. The +1.63% online revenue belongs to the full system. Local tests check loss and gradients, not causal business gains.

Sources: [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md) · [KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If ESMM uses MMoE or PLE instead of two towers, can we stop distinguishing CVR and CTCVR? {#cross-probability-chain-versus-expert-sharing}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MMoE and PLE change parameter sharing, not probability semantics. CVR is conditional on click; CTCVR is the joint post-impression event of click and conversion. A flexible network cannot mix these labels or turn non-clicks into conditional CVR negatives.

    **Illustrative example:** From 1,000 impressions, 100 clicks, and 20 conversions, CTR is 10%, conditional CVR is 20%, and CTCVR is 2%. Expert gating does not equalize the denominators.

    Sources: [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md) · [Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts](../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en.md) · [Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en.md)

### If MMoE already has per-task gates, why add task-specific experts in PLE? {#cross-gates-versus-private-paths}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** MMoE changes gates but still mixes shared experts. Gradients can conflict in the same parameters. PLE adds private transforms while preserving a shared path. This changes the sharing boundary; it does not guarantee better scores on every task.

    **Illustrative example:** Click prediction may favor attention-grabbing titles while satisfaction penalizes clickbait. Two gates using the same expert can still compete; private paths preserve some separate processing.

    Sources: [Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts](../../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en.md) · [Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/recsys2020-ple-ple/README-en.md)

### If FLVM predicts a user likes content, why might Incrementality decide not to contact them? {#cross-engagement-not-incrementality}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** FLVM estimates a latent value direction behind feedback. An intervention must consider whether the user would consume anyway. Incrementality compares potential-outcome differences and uncertainty under a budget. Users with high natural preference can have little uplift.

    **Illustrative example:** A user's return rate rises from 90% to 92% with contact, another from 10% to 20%. The first has greater absolute return, the second greater uplift. These are illustrative numbers.

    Sources: [Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en.md) · [From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en.md)

### Why not recalculate the two teacher weights from the current student at each step? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Alpha is calibrated from the fixed initial policy, making it part of the fixed training objective. Dynamic recalculation changes both objective and gradient semantics. A dynamic variant may work but needs separate validation.

    **Illustrative example:** An initial 1:3 gap gives weights 1/4 and 3/4. Keep them even if later gaps change.

    Sources: [Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate](../../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en.md) · [KL-MOPD: Discrepancy-Aware Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.36973-kl-mopd/README-en.md)
